I see the justification for `delete` vs `memdelete`, but none for the `emscripten_cancel_main_loop()`. As far as I can tell this call is causing some trouble when closing a game session in the web editor, as I end up with this being emitted into my VS Code debug console when doing so:

(I don't quite understand why it doesn't show up in my browser's console though. I only ever see it in VS Code's debug console when launching Chrome using a VS Code `"type": "chrome"` launch configuration.) I figured this was just a harmless error at first, but I'm currently hunting down a memory leak in the web editor that only shows up when `use_assertions=yes` is passed, and which disappears when using `use_assertions=no`, and this `emscripten_cancel_main_loop()` call seems to be the culprit somehow, as removing it makes both the assertion and memory leak go away.

I see, I think it was to remove the spam of errors if the engine failed to shut down before `emscripten_force_exit` was called, because that spam of errors made the original error hard to track down. If it's not needed it can be removed, also it seems to still cause the error spam in VS Code's debug, so it doesn't help here?

Also I think if the memory leak is coming from calling `emscripten_cancel_main_loop` before `emscripten_force_exit` it should really be emscripten bug.

@mihe I tested it more in a simple project and it seems I overthought the safety by adding `emscripten_cancel_main_loop`, it was really unneeded. 

Well after looking at the emscripten's tests, there are a couple of those that use the same pattern, so it seems what I was doing is not something too unusual, but I'm just wondering why it didn't got caught here. I created the issue with more info here https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/issues/27456 . The one that appeared here is listed as the `Error 2`.

All of the checking code is stripped without assertions, so it only affects things when assertions are enabled. And yeah it seems strange that the error is only surfaced in the VS Code's debug or a simple project, but not in the browser itself, so maybe there are also a couple of more subtle bugs here. But `emscripten_cancel_main_loop` should be removed.

I basically thought it wouldn't hurt to be extra sure that exiting loop won't be called again, so I chose to cancel the exiting loop before exiting the runtime, logically to me it made sense `running -> stop -> exit`. I was wrong.

Thank you for taking a closer look, and for filing an upstream issue about it.

> But `emscripten_cancel_main_loop` should be removed.

Would you mind putting up a PR for it, or should I do it?

You should do it, yeah. You already tested locally that it resolves your issue, and for me to test it I would need to compile Godot several times, which takes too long on my laptop if the changes are already tested.

@NoctemCat I've put up the PR for removing `emscripten_cancel_main_loop`: #122056

I focused the issue around the assertion instead of the memory leak, which apparently does show up just fine in Firefox, just not in Chrome (for me at least).

~~If you're able/willing, a PR review from you would probably go a long way towards getting that fix merged, since you introduced the `emscripten_cancel_main_loop` call.~~

EDIT: Nevermind, looks like it got approved as I was typing up this comment.
